claim: Randall states that in the passage narrating Darien's death in The Darkest Road the sentences are short and the description concrete.
quote: Sentences are short, description is concrete.

claim: Randall describes the tone of that same Darien death passage as matter-of-fact.
quote: The tone, moreover, is matter-of-fact.

claim: Randall reads the passage narrating the departure of Arthur, Lancelot and Guinevere as a deliberate reach for rhetorical high style, in contrast with the plain Darien passage.
quote: the language here is an obvious attempt at rhetorical

claim: Randall explains the elevated register of the Arthurian departure scene as a consequence of who perceives it, not of the event's importance.
quote: because it is perceived by minds capable of comprehending magnificence

claim: Randall counts twenty-six different agents of focalization in The Fionavar Tapestry.
quote: employs twenty-six different agents of focalization
page: opening section, before 'Assimilating the Secondary World'

claim: Randall counts twenty-one shifts of focalization in the eighth chapter of The Summer Tree.
quote: shifts focalization twenty-one times

claim: Randall counts eighty-seven shifts of focalization across Darien's search for Rakoth, with Darien himself the focalizant only nine of those times.
quote: the narrative shifts focalization eighty-seven times

claim: Randall argues that Kay's shifts of focalization delay the unfolding of the story as well as advancing it.
quote: the shifts delay the unfolding of the story

claim: Randall argues the reader must assemble Kay's secondary world by inference from the successive focalizations rather than from direct exposition.
quote: Our task is to piece together the world by understanding the focalizations.

claim: James Gunn writes that Kay's novels stand out for their richness of character and fullness of scene.
source: James Gunn, Easton Press introduction to Tigana, 30 July 1998
quote: richness of character, their fullness of scene
page: introduction, paragraph beginning 'That describes Tigana as well.'

claim: Gunn says Tigana reads like a richly tapestried historical novel dense with character and detail.
source: James Gunn, Easton Press introduction to Tigana, 30 July 1998
quote: dense with character and detail

claim: Gunn credits Kay's willingness to kill major characters with giving Tigana the edge of reality against what might otherwise be airily fantastic.
source: James Gunn, Easton Press introduction to Tigana, 30 July 1998
quote: gives the edge of reality to what might otherwise be airily fantastic

claim: Cobb argues that the enrichment Kay's historical fantasy offers its readers is primarily emotional rather than rational.
quote: primarily emotional rather than rational

claim: Cobb states that in Tigana the past cannot be changed but history, meaning the memory and the record of the past, can be changed.
quote: the past cannot be changed, but history

claim: Janeen Webb characterises the plotting of A Song for Arbonne as political survival ungarlanded by personal myth, in contrast to Tigana.
source: Janeen Webb, critic, The New York Review of Science Fiction
quote: political survival ungarlanded by personal myth
page: section comparing Tigana and A Song for Arbonne

claim: Rettino argues that Kay's narrator at times sounds like a historian because of the distance at which it relates events.
quote: whose voice at times resembles that of a historian in its distanced relation of events
page: section on Tigana and the club-story

claim: Rettino reads the narrator of Under Heaven as presenting himself as one Kitan historian among many.
quote: The narrator presents himself as one Kitan historian among many.

claim: Rettino observes that Kay slides world information into a character's thoughts, disguising the narrator's exposition as Jehane's thinking in The Lions of Al-Rassan.
quote: The narrator subtly offers information to the reader, disguising it as Jehane
page: section on The Lions of Al-Rassan

claim: Kay says one starting point of Children of Earth and Sky was that it takes place on the borderlands in the lives of not-powerful people.
